# Skills in OUM

Status: implemented in v0.3.0. `base_hash` enforces read-before-write.

OpenCode owns discovery, the `/skills` picker, and the `skill` loader. OUM owns
authoring and curation only. It never implements a library, picker, viewer, or
loader.

## Ownership

| Concern | Owner |
|---|---|
| Discover skills | OpenCode (`ctx.skill.list()`, `/api/skill`) |
| Show/select in the TUI | OpenCode `/skills` |
| Load a skill body | OpenCode `skill` tool |
| Create/patch a skill | OUM `oum_skill_manage` |
| Decide what to create | OUM learn module |
| Dedupe and candidate selection | OUM internal index |
| Provenance and audit | OUM frontmatter + ledger |

## Roots

| Scope | Path | OUM writes |
|---|---|---|
| global | `~/.agents/skills` | promote / global create |
| project | `<project>/.opencode/skills` | project create / fork |
| native global | `~/.config/opencode/skills` | no (left to the user) |
| compat | `.claude/skills`, project `.agents/skills` | no |

`.agents/skills` is the canonical global library because that is where the
existing library lives and it is portable across agents. Configurable via
`skills.globalRoot`.

## Advertised, not loaded

OpenCode advertises only ID, name, and description. A body loads only when the
model calls `skill` or the user picks it via `/skills`. OUM does not hide skills
by default. `metadata.opencode/autoinvoke: false` is an explicit opt-in.

Descriptions are the retrieval key. OUM enforces
`skills.descriptionBudget` (default 200 chars) and requires a specific,
action-oriented description.

## Layout

```text
<root>/[category/]<id>/SKILL.md
<root>/[category/]<id>/references/<topic>.md
<root>/[category/]<id>/templates/<name>.<ext>
<root>/[category/]<id>/scripts/<name>.<ext>
```

- Directory form only.
- IDs are lowercase kebab-case, 1–64 chars, matching the directory.
- No state, ledgers, backups, temp files, or hidden directories inside the
  library. Those live under `<dataRoot>`:
  - `state.db`
  - `skills-ledger.jsonl`
  - `skill-backups/<hash>/`
  - `skill-archive/`

## Frontmatter

```yaml
---
name: Git Release
description: Prepare release notes, version bumps, and GitHub releases
metadata:
  oum:
    origin: self | user | fork | compat
    scope: global | project
    created: 2026-10-21
    updated: 2026-10-21
    pinned: false
    promoted_from: <project id or path>
---
```

OpenCode ignores `metadata.oum`. `origin: user` skills are never patched by the
learn module unless `skills.editUserSkills` is true.

## Actions

`oum_skill_manage`:

- `create`
- `patch`
- `write_file`
- `remove_file`
- `delete` (archives)
- `promote`
- `fork`

Guards:

- Read-before-write for patch/delete.
- Path safety: no `..`, no absolute paths, no symlink escape.
- Duplicate name refusal.
- Size and frontmatter validation.
- Description budget.
- Ledger append.
- `ctx.skill.reload()` after every mutation.
- Collision with a higher-precedence source is refused, not overwritten.

## Promote and fork

- `promote`: move `<project>/.opencode/skills/<id>` to the global root. Refuse if
  the ID exists globally (offer patch). Detect a project-local duplicate and
  explain precedence. Record `promoted_from` and `promoted_at`.
- `fork`: copy a global skill into the current project, mark `origin: fork`.
  Project precedence makes the fork win locally.

## Scope policy

- Project-specific procedure → project root.
- Portable class-level technique → global root.
- Ambiguous → project root; promote later on demand.
- The learn module never promotes silently.

## Learn module interactions

- The learn module receives candidate skill bodies as **input**. It does not get
  a read tool.
- It may patch `origin: self` and `origin: fork` skills by default.
- It creates class-level umbrellas, never session-artifact names.
- It must honor `POLICY.md` over the transcript.
- A changed decision must supersede or patch the old skill; contradictory
  guidance is a bug.

## Clean-library rules

- Dedupe before create; patch an existing umbrella instead of adding a near
  duplicate.
- Keep global skills portable; no project paths or secrets.
- Descriptions are short and specific; bodies can be rich.
- Archive, don't hard-delete, user-authored skills.

# OpenUltraMem (OUM)

Memory that survives the session — for OpenCode V2.

OUM adds three things to OpenCode:

- **Canonical memory** — bounded `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md`, plus a private
  per-project file, injected as a stable per-session snapshot.
- **Session recall** — a disposable `state.db` index over OpenCode's own session
  history, with ranked full-text search.
- **Procedural memory** — learn-driven skill authoring into OpenCode's native
  skill roots, with provenance, dedupe, and promotion.

OpenCode remains the source of truth. Every OUM index is derived, disposable, and
rebuildable. No embeddings, no duplicated transcripts, no V1 compatibility layer.

Status: **v0.4.0** — retrieval, canonical memory, the learn module, and skill
authoring are built and tested, and OUM has replaced `opencode-hermes` on the
author's machine ([docs/MIGRATION.md](docs/MIGRATION.md)). Next: live use,
consolidation quality, and the 1.0 decision.

## Install

OpenCode V2 only (tested on 2.2.0). Add the plugin to `opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["file:///home/you/Projects/openultramem"]
}
```

Nothing else is required: the plugin ships TypeScript sources and runs inside
OpenCode's Bun runtime. Configuration is read from plugin `options` or `OUM_*`
environment variables — for example:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "file:///home/you/Projects/openultramem",
      "options": { "memoryRoot": "~/.config/opencode/oum" }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `~/.config/opencode/oum/MEMORY.md`, `USER.md` | machine-wide canonical memory; survives everything |
| `~/.config/opencode/oum/projects/<id>/MEMORY.md` | private per-project facts, injected only there |
| `~/.config/opencode/oum/POLICY.md` | user-owned rules the learn module must obey |
| `~/.local/share/opencode/oum/state.db` | derived session index; safe to delete |
| `~/.local/share/opencode/oum/oum.log` | diagnostics (no TUI toasts) |

Do not run OUM and `opencode-hermes` together: both inject a memory block and
write the same files. OUM warns and skips injection while hermes is active
unless `coexistence: true`.

See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the architecture, the native-interop
contract, the data schema, and the milestones. Release history is in
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

# Changelog

Semantic versioning. Tags are annotated (`v0.1.0`) and always match
`package.json` and `src/version.ts`.

## 0.5.1 — 2026-10-27

- **Fix: project memory key.** Keying by `project.id` alone is wrong — local-only
  repositories share the global project id, so two unrelated local directories
  would read each other's project memory. The key is now
  `<project-id>-<hash(canonical directory)>`, which the original design had
  already called out as the trap.
- Config-root project files written under the old key are empty and were removed.

## 0.5.0 — 2026-10-27

Project-scoped memory.

- **Third target** — `oum_memory` accepts `target: "project"`, backed by
  `<memoryRoot>/projects/<project-id>/MEMORY.md` with its own budget
  (`projectChars`, default 1,200). It is injected after the global pair and only
  for sessions in that project.
- **Private by construction** — the file lives under the config root, never in the
  repository, so project facts cannot leak into a public repo. Absolute paths are
  allowed there and still forbidden in global memory.
- **Learn scope rule** — plans choose `project` for project-specific conventions,
  commands, layout, and gotchas, and `memory`/`user` for machine-wide facts.
  Ambiguous goes to `project`: a scoped fact cannot pollute other projects.
- **Frozen like the rest** — the project block is read once per session; a
  mid-session write appears in new sessions only.

## 0.4.1 — 2026-10-27

- **Attributable learn events.** Every trigger and run record now carries the
  plugin instance id. A repeated prompt hook and a second plugin instance look
  identical in the log without it; now they do not.
- Context: after the migration, `prompt` hooks fired more than once for one turn
  (V2 documents this as possible), producing rows with contradictory counters.
  No duplicate memory injection was observed — a fresh session saw exactly one
  MEMORY and one USER block.

## 0.4.0 — 2026-10-27

Migration, and the end of `opencode-hermes` on this machine.

- **`scripts/migrate.ts`** — dry-run inspection and `--apply` copy of canonical
  memory. Additive by policy: it refuses a non-empty target unless `--force`,
  backs the target up first, and verifies entry counts after copying.
- **`src/migrate.ts`** — the reusable plan/apply/verify logic behind it, with
  conflict detection between source and target.
- **Live migration** — memory consolidated from 2,184 to 1,892 chars (11 entries,
  308 headroom), `POLICY.md` written, `opencode.jsonc` switched from
  `opencode-hermes` to `openultramem`, and every check in `docs/MIGRATION.md`
  verified on a private server.
- **Documented operational detail** — the running service caches its plugin set,
  so `opencode service restart` is required for sessions that were open during
  the switch; new locations load OUM immediately.

## 0.3.0 — 2026-10-27

Procedural memory: OUM can author skills in OpenCode's own roots.

- **`oum_skill_manage`** — `create`, `patch`, `write_file`, `remove_file`,
  `delete`, `promote`, `fork`, with guards: kebab-case ids, a description budget,
  path safety (no `..`, no absolute paths, no symlink escape), and size limits.
- **Provenance** — `metadata.oum` records origin (`self`/`user`/`fork`/`compat`),
  scope, created/updated dates, pinning, and `promoted_from`. Files without it
  are treated as user-authored and left alone unless `skills.editUserSkills`.
- **Read-before-write** — `patch` and `delete` require `base_hash`. When it is
  missing the tool returns the current body and sha; the hash is the same one
  discovery reports, so it stays valid across calls and sessions.
- **Nothing is destroyed** — edits back up the skill directory, deletes move it
  to `skill-archive/`, and every mutation appends to `skills-ledger.jsonl`.
- **Promote and fork** — promote moves a project skill to the global library and
  records where it came from; fork copies a global skill into the project so
  project precedence wins locally. Learn plans may never promote.
- **Learn integration** — candidates now arrive with scope, sha, and body, so the
  engine can patch an umbrella precisely; `promote` remains an explicit action.
- **Dedupe index** — a `skills` table plus FTS in `state.db` surfaces near
  duplicates before a create, and is never exposed as a tool.

Known limitation: `globalRoot` must be a root OpenCode natively discovers
(`~/.agents/skills` by default). Pointing it elsewhere keeps the skill out of
`/skills` until it is promoted or the root is discovered.

## 0.2.0 — 2026-10-27

The learning loop: OUM now writes memory instead of waiting to be asked.

- **Learn module** — trigger accounting on user turns and tool calls, a per-session
  throttle, one in-flight run with a reasoned dirty bit, and turn-end boundaries
  from `session.execution.*`. A missed execution event is caught by the next
  prompt (the mandatory fallback).
- **Structured plans** — one pinned-model completion returns strict JSON
  (`memory`, `curation`, `skills`), validated field by field with one corrective
  retry. The engine never writes; the host applies.
- **Policy precedence** — `POLICY.md` is an input and outranks the transcript, so
  a mid-conversation decision cannot be encoded over a standing rule.
- **Curation** — `supersede`, `merge`, and `archive`/`demote` map onto memory
  edits; `promote` is refused until note scopes exist.
- **Idempotency** — every applied operation is hashed into `state.db`, so a
  retried run cannot duplicate a fact.
- **Observability** — `learn-events.jsonl` records every trigger decision with a
  reason and every run with model, counts, duration, and errors; `bun run
  scripts/summary.ts` prints the weekly shape.
- **`/oum-reflect`** — a command that forces a review, bypassing counters and
  throttle but never the in-flight guard.

## 0.1.0 — 2026-10-27

First release: the two halves of memory that do not need a model.

- **Session recall** — disposable `state.db` index over OpenCode's own V2 history.
  Contentless word + trigram FTS5, reciprocal rank fusion, bodies hydrated from
  the host read-only. `oum_session_search` covers discovery, scroll, read, and
  browse; search falls back to a bounded `LIKE` when the index is stale.
- **Canonical memory** — bounded `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` with `§` entries, atomic
  writes, a lock file, and per-entry budget refusals instead of silent
  truncation. `oum_memory` supports add, replace, remove, and atomic batch.
- **Frozen snapshot** — the memory block is read once per session and reused for
  every request, so a mid-session write cannot change the prompt under the model.
- **First-run migration** — copies `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` from `opencode-hermes`
  when the OUM roots are empty; never overwrites.
- **Coexistence guard** — warns and skips injection while `opencode-hermes` is
  active, unless `coexistence: true`.
- **Verification** — the four OpenCode 2.2.0 unknowns are measured and recorded
  in `docs/VERIFICATION.md`; 38 tests plus a 10k-message benchmark (query p95
  15 ms against a 50 ms budget).

Not in this release: the learn module (M3), skills (M4), and migration
completion (M5).

- No changes to native tools, prompts, models, compaction, or skills discovery.

# OpenUltraMem (OUM) — Design

Status: design locked 2026-10-21. Not implemented.
Target: OpenCode V2 only. V1 is out of scope.

## 1. What it is

A V2-native memory system for OpenCode with three parts:

1. **Canonical memory** — bounded `MEMORY.md` + `USER.md`, injected as a frozen
   per-session snapshot.
2. **Session recall** — a disposable `state.db` index over OpenCode's own
   session history, with ranked full-text search.
3. **Procedural memory** — learn-driven skill authoring into OpenCode's native
   skill roots, with provenance, dedupe, and promotion.

The source of truth is always OpenCode's database and the Markdown files. Every
OUM index is derived, disposable, and rebuildable.

## 2. Non-goals

- Embeddings / vector recall in v1.
- A model-powered controller backend in v1 (interface only; see Appendix A).
- V1 session history or the V1 plugin API.
- Cross-tool (non-OpenCode) history.
- A parallel skill registry, picker, or loader.
- Cloud sync, GUI, or a daemon.

## 3. Canonical memory

- Files: `<memoryRoot>/MEMORY.md` (2,200 chars) and `<memoryRoot>/USER.md`
  (1,375 chars). Entries joined by `\n§\n`, same format as Hermes.
- Per-project memory: `<memoryRoot>/projects/<project-key>/MEMORY.md`
  (`projectChars`, default 1,200), where the key is the project id plus a hash of
  the canonical directory — local-only repositories share the id, not the path. Injected after the global pair, scoped to the
  project that owns the session. It lives under the config root, never in the
  repository, so project facts cannot leak into a public repo. Absolute paths are
  allowed there and forbidden in the global files.
- `<memoryRoot>/POLICY.md`: user-owned design decisions and scope rules, read by
  the learn module. It is not injected into the session; it exists so the writer
  does not encode stale intermediate decisions.
- `memoryRoot` defaults to `~/.config/opencode/oum`. A migration copies the old
  `~/.config/opencode/memories` files on first run if the new root is empty.
- **Frozen snapshot:** at `session.created`, read both files and cache the
  rendered block by session ID. The `context` hook appends that exact text on
  every model request for the session. Mid-session file edits hit disk but do not
  change the prompt. Evict on `session.deleted`.
- **Tool:** `oum_memory` with `add`, `replace`, `remove`, `batch`; targets
  `memory`, `user`, and `project`.
  - `add` refuses when the target is over budget and returns per-entry sizes plus
    a consolidation instruction.
  - `replace` and `remove` match `old_text` exactly once.
  - Batch operations apply atomically.
- **Writes:** temp file + fsync + rename, guarded by a lock file. A write that
  observes an external change re-reads and re-plans before applying.
- **Validation:** reject entries containing the `§` delimiter, empty entries, and
  content matching the prompt-injection scanner.
- No `demote`, no vector mirror. If a fact matters it belongs in the file; if it
  does not, session search finds the transcript.

## 4. Session recall

### 4.1 Store

`state.db` at `<dataRoot>/state.db`, WAL, `synchronous=NORMAL`,
`busy_timeout=5000`. `dataRoot` defaults to `~/.local/share/opencode/oum`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);

CREATE TABLE sessions(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  project_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  directory TEXT NOT NULL,
  title TEXT,
  parent_id TEXT,
  model TEXT,
  created INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated INTEGER NOT NULL,
  hidden INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  indexed_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE messages(
  rid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
  role TEXT NOT NULL,          -- user | assistant | tool | synthetic
  created INTEGER NOT NULL,
  tool_name TEXT,
  chars INTEGER NOT NULL,
  indexed_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- Word index: BM25 and phrase precision. Contentless: tokens only.
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE messages_fts USING fts5(
  text,
  content='', contentless_delete=1,
  tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'
);

-- Substring index: literal matching and high recall. Contentless: tokens only.
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE messages_fts_tri USING fts5(
  text,
  content='', contentless_delete=1,
  tokenize='trigram'
);

CREATE INDEX messages_session_seq ON messages(session_id, seq);
CREATE INDEX messages_created ON messages(created);
```

The indexes are contentless. Full message bodies are hydrated from
`opencode.db` by message ID. Deleting `state.db` loses no history.

### 4.2 Ingest

V2 only: `session_v2` + `session_message`.

- `user` → `data.text`.
- `assistant` → text blocks; tool blocks become role `tool` rows with the tool
  name and a bounded prefix of input/output. Reasoning blocks are skipped.
- `synthetic` → include unless it is an OUM/provider recall note; compaction
  summaries are included as `synthetic`.
- `system`, `idle`, `location-switched` → skipped.
- `session_v2.parent_id` children are `hidden = 1`; searchable only with
  `include_children: true`.

Watermark: `(time_created, id)` in `meta`. Every sync re-scans a 60-second
overlap window; upserts are idempotent by message ID. Each message upsert
deletes and reinserts its FTS rows by `rid` in the same transaction.

Deletions: purge on `session.deleted` and on a full reconcile pass. A reconcile
compares mirror session IDs against the host.

Sync is bounded (`search.syncBudgetMs`, default 250 ms). If it fails or exceeds
the budget, search proceeds on the existing index and reports `stale: true`.

### 4.3 Search

1. Sync (bounded).
2. Word FTS and trigram FTS in parallel, top 50 each.
3. Reciprocal rank fusion (`k = 60`), dedupe by message ID, recency tiebreak.
4. Hydrate top hits from `opencode.db`; build snippets around the match.
5. Fallback to a bounded `LIKE` query over extracted host text if both indexes
   are empty or stale.

Modes: `broad` (OR terms, default), `exact` (phrase / substring).

### 4.4 Tool

`oum_session_search` keeps the Hermes shape:

- `query` → discovery.
- `session_id` + `around_message_id` → scroll.
- `session_id` alone → read.
- no args → browse.

Extra fields: `limit`, `detail` (`summary` | `full`), `include_children`,
`project`. Results include session ID, title, directory, time, matched role,
message ID, snippet, and a `@session/local/<id>` link.

## 5. Skills

OpenCode owns discovery, the `/skills` picker, and the `skill` loader. OUM owns
authoring and curation only.

### 5.1 Roots

| Scope         | Path                                       | OUM writes              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- |
| global        | `~/.agents/skills`                         | promote / global create |
| project       | `<project>/.opencode/skills`               | project create / fork   |
| native global | `~/.config/opencode/skills`                | no (left to the user)   |
| compat        | `.claude/skills`, project `.agents/skills` | no                      |

`.agents/skills` is the canonical global library because that is where the
existing library lives and it is portable across agents. It is configurable via
`skills.globalRoot`.

### 5.2 Advertised, not loaded

OpenCode advertises only ID, name, and description. A body loads only when the
model calls `skill` or the user picks it via `/skills`. OUM does not hide skills
by default; `metadata.opencode/autoinvoke: false` is an explicit opt-in, not a
policy.

Descriptions are the retrieval key. OUM enforces `skills.descriptionBudget`
(default 200 chars) and requires a specific, action-oriented description.

### 5.3 Layout and cleanliness

- Directory form only: `<root>/[category/]<id>/SKILL.md` plus `references/`,
  `templates/`, `scripts/`.
- IDs are lowercase kebab-case, 1–64 chars, matching the directory.
- No state, ledgers, backups, temp files, or hidden directories inside the
  library. Those live under `<dataRoot>`:
  - `state.db`
  - `skills-ledger.jsonl`
  - `skill-backups/<hash>/`
  - `skill-archive/`
- Deleting a skill archives it to `<dataRoot>/skill-archive/`; it never
  hard-deletes a user-authored skill.
- Collisions: if the same ID exists in a higher-precedence source
  (`~/.config/opencode/skills`, project scope, explicit `skills` entries), OUM
  warns and refuses to create; the user chooses patch, fork, or rename.

### 5.4 Scope policy

- Project-specific procedure → project root.
- Portable class-level technique → global root.
- Ambiguous → project root; promote later on demand.
- The learn module never promotes silently.

### 5.5 Promote and fork

- `promote`: move `<project>/.opencode/skills/<id>` to the global root. Refuse if
  the ID exists globally (offer patch). Detect a project-local duplicate and
  explain precedence. Record `promoted_from` and `promoted_at`.
- `fork`: copy a global skill into the current project, mark
  `origin: fork`. Project precedence makes the fork win locally.

### 5.6 Frontmatter

```yaml
---
name: Git Release
description: Prepare release notes, version bumps, and GitHub releases
metadata:
  oum:
    origin: self | user | fork | compat
    scope: global | project
    created: 2026-10-21
    updated: 2026-10-21
    pinned: false
    promoted_from: <project id or path>
---
```

OpenCode ignores `metadata.oum`. `origin: user` skills are never patched by the
learn module unless `skills.editUserSkills` is true.

### 5.7 Tool

`oum_skill_manage` actions:

- `create`, `patch`, `write_file`, `remove_file`
- `delete` (archives)
- `promote`, `fork`

Guards: read-before-write for patch/delete, path safety (no `..`, no absolute
paths, no symlink escape), duplicate name refusal, size and frontmatter
validation, ledger append, `ctx.skill.reload()` after every mutation.

### 5.8 Index

Internal only: a `skills` table + FTS in `state.db`. Used for dedupe before
create and for candidate selection in the learn module. Not exposed as a tool. Native
advertising is the search.

## 6. Learn module

The learn module is the memory system's writer: it decides what to save, what to
consolidate, and which skills to create or patch. It is a module, not a hook
callback, because the decision logic must be testable without a live host.

### 6.1 Contract

```ts
interface LearnEngine {
  plan(input: LearnInput): Promise<LearnPlan>
}

interface LearnInput {
  transcript: Transcript
  project: ProjectContext
  memory: MemorySnapshot
  skills: SkillCandidate[]
  policy: string
  budget: LearnBudget
}

interface LearnPlan {
  memory: MemoryOperation[]
  skills: SkillOperation[]
  curation: CurationOperation[]
  notes?: string
  confidence?: number
}
```

The host applies the plan; the engine never writes. `apply(plan)` is
transactional, idempotent per operation hash, and validates every operation
against the current store before applying.

### 6.2 Triggers

- Memory nudge: every `learn.triggers.turns` user turns (default 10), counted in
  `prompt`.
- Skill nudge: every `learn.triggers.toolIterations` tool calls (default 10), counted in
  `tool.execute.after`.
- Turn end: `session.execution.succeeded | failed | interrupted`. If the event
  stream misses it, the **next `prompt` hook** reviews the previous turn. This
  fallback is mandatory.
- Compaction: enqueue a flush; do not block or replace compaction.
- Manual: `/oum-reflect` forces a review.
- Coalesce: one in-flight learn run per session; newer triggers set a dirty bit.

Every trigger decision is logged with a reason: `due`, `not-due:turns`,
`not-due:throttle`, `not-due:in-flight`, `skipped:model`, `skipped:disabled`.

### 6.3 Execution

A single `generate.text` call, pinned to the reviewed session's model. If the
model cannot be resolved, skip and log; never fall back silently to a global
default.

Input: a bounded transcript (`learn.maxTranscriptChars`, default 60,000 chars)
built from user text, assistant text, tool names and bounded tool results.
Reasoning is stripped. The plugin reads candidate skill bodies from disk and
includes them; the engine **does not get a read tool**, so there are no
permission errors and no exploratory reads.

Output: strict JSON matching `LearnPlan`. Validation is strict. Apply in one
transaction; retry once with the validation error appended. A failed learn run
never throws into the host.

### 6.4 Policy input

The engine receives the current `POLICY.md` (design decisions, conventions,
scope rules) and the current MEMORY/notes index. **Policy beats transcript.**
If the conversation appears to contradict the current policy, the engine flags
it instead of writing a skill that encodes the old decision.

This exists because the V2 run captured a mid-conversation statement
("never write to `~/.agents/skills`") that a later decision reversed. Without a
policy input, skills encode stale guidance.

### 6.5 Curation

The learn plan can include curation operations:

- `supersede(old, new)` — new note/skill wins; old is marked, not silently kept.
- `merge(a, b)` — consolidate near-duplicates, preserving provenance.
- `demote(note)` — move an always-on fact to a note, or mark it stale.
- `promote(note)` — move a project fact to global (only with a promote policy).
- `archive(note)` — remove from active retrieval; keep the evidence.

The engine proposes; the host validates and applies. A reconcile pass on
startup and compaction rebuilds indexes from canonical files and flags orphans.

### 6.6 Observability

Append one JSONL record per trigger and per run to
`<dataRoot>/learn-events.jsonl`:

```json
{"ts":"...","session":"...","event":"trigger","reason":"due","turns":12,"tools":31}
{"ts":"...","session":"...","event":"run","durationMs":24000,"model":"...","memory":2,"skills":2,"errors":[],"tokens":{}}
```

A weekly summary logs runs, writes, dedupe rate, stale rate, and skipped
reasons. No TUI toasts.

### 6.7 Prompts

- Memory: declarative facts only — environment, conventions, corrections,
  stable preferences. No procedures; procedures belong in skills. Respect the
  budget and consolidate rather than overflow.
- Skills: class-level umbrellas; patch a loaded skill first, then an existing
  umbrella, then add a support file, then create. Strong description. Decide
  scope. Never invent session-artifact names.
- Both: "nothing to save" is allowed but not the default; no secrets, no
  transcripts, no one-off task state.

### 6.8 Lessons from the V2 run

The 2026-10-21 V2 run produced a good class-level skill and two memory entries,
and consolidated to stay under the cap. It also exposed the failure modes this
module must fix:

- The trigger is the product: one run in three days is not learning.
- Silence is the default failure: no skip log means no diagnosis.
- Read tools in a restricted review session produce avoidable errors; pass the
  files instead.
- Mid-conversation decisions get captured; policy must be an input.
- Consolidation works; keep it, and make it observable.

## 7. Native interop contract

| V2 surface | OUM behavior |
|---|---|
| Tool catalog | 3 namespaced tools, registered once at setup. No conditional tools. |
| Code Mode | `codemode: true`, namespace `oum`. |
| Tool descriptions | Compact; enums; `additionalProperties: false`. |
| Context hook | Only append the frozen memory block to `event.system`. |
| Prompt hook | Count turns only. Never rewrite the prompt. |
| Compaction | Read and enqueue. Never set `event.result` or edit messages. |
| Event stream | Queue work only; bounded queue; drain worker; reconnect with backoff. |
| Session lifecycle | Never create, remove, move, rename, or reprompt a user session. |
| Host DB | Read-only attach (`mode=ro`). Never write OpenCode's database. |
| Model/provider | Never set model, provider, headers, or request options. |
| Native skills | Write only to OUM roots; call `ctx.skill.reload()` after writes. |
| Existing skills | Learn module edits `origin: self|fork` only by default. |
| Permissions | Every tool calls `ctx.permission.assert`; no blanket deny; no bypass. |
| Coexistence | If `opencode-hermes` is active, log and disable unless explicitly allowed. |
| Failure isolation | Every hook wrapped; sync/search time-bounded; corrupt index recreated. |
| UI | Log only. No toasts, titles, or session metadata. |

## Appendix A. Optional controller backend (Jev / Laya)

Status: deferred; interface only in v1.

OUM's memory decisions are structured: what to save, which scope, whether it is
a duplicate, how notes relate, how to route a query, and when evidence is
sufficient. v1 uses deterministic rules plus FTS. A model-powered controller can
replace the rules later without changing the store or the plugin surface.

### A.1 Interface

```ts
interface MemoryController {
  classify(note: Observation, ctx: DecisionContext): Promise<Classification>
  relate(note: Observation, candidates: Note[]): Promise<NoteEdge[]>
  route(query: string, ctx: DecisionContext): Promise<QueryRoute>
  score(query: string, candidates: Chunk[]): Promise<CandidateScore[]>
  assess(query: string, evidence: Chunk[]): Promise<EvidenceAssessment>
  consolidate(note: Note, neighbors: Note[]): Promise<ConsolidationPlan>
}
```

- `RuleController` is the default.
- `LayaController` uses the local `laya-serve` endpoint
  (`POST /v1/systemone`) with typed Noul/Choice questions. Local only.
- `JevController` uses the hosted TypeSafe API. Disabled by default; explicit
  opt-in with a data-egress warning.

### A.2 Rules

1. **Advisory only.** The controller proposes; OUM validates and applies. It
   never writes memory, skills, or files directly.
2. **Bounded.** A maximum number of decisions per learn run, a per-call timeout,
   and fail-open to `RuleController`.
3. **Local by default.** No project data leaves the machine. Hosted Jev requires
   an explicit, documented opt-in.
4. **Reproducible.** Store backend ID, model hash, and decision-schema version
   with every applied decision.
5. **Off the critical path.** Run at ingest, learn, and compaction; cache
   results. Never on the per-request path.
6. **Earned, not assumed.** Enable only after a labeled benchmark beats the rule
   baseline on decision accuracy and learn quality. Laya base checkpoints are
   near chance zero-shot on typed decisions (0.362 vs a 0.461 majority-class
   baseline in the model card); fine-tuning and temperature calibration are
   prerequisites, not optional.

### A.3 What to borrow from Jev-Mem

- Typed decisions with bounded output spaces, batched.
- Preserve canonical observations with provenance; defer selectivity to
  retrieval.
- Hybrid anchors, bounded expansion, and explicit stopping (sufficiency,
  expected utility, contradiction).
- Periodic consolidation for redundancy, contradiction, and obsolescence.
- Decision traces for debugging.

### A.4 What not to borrow

- The full four-view graph in v1. Start with a small relation layer:
  `depends_on`, `supersedes`, `caused_by`, `same_module`, `fixes`.
- The hosted Jev API for private code.
- LoCoMo-tuned thresholds or benchmark claims.

# Migrating from `opencode-hermes`

Status: **completed 2026-10-27** on OpenCode 2.2.0. This document stays as the
record and the rollback plan.

## What was done

1. Backed up `~/.config/opencode/memories`, `~/.agents/skills`, `opencode.jsonc`,
   and the OUM root to `~/.config/opencode/backups/oum-migration-<timestamp>`.
2. Consolidated `MEMORY.md` from 2,184 to 1,892 chars (11 entries, 308 headroom)
   without dropping a fact; copied the result to both roots so a rollback is
   consistent.
3. Wrote `~/.config/opencode/oum/POLICY.md` (memory scope, skill scope, version
   and migration rules, coexistence).
4. Ran `bun run scripts/migrate.ts --apply --force`. It copied `MEMORY.md` and
   `USER.md`, verified entry counts after the copy, and backed up the target.
5. Replaced the `opencode-hermes` plugin entry with `openultramem` in
   `opencode.jsonc`; `opencode-jev` was left untouched.
6. Verified on a fresh server (`opencode run --standalone`): one memory block
   (86% / 94%), all three OUM tools, session search hits, memory add/remove back
   to baseline, a skill created → loaded by the native `skill` tool → archived,
   and a learn trigger and run in `learn-events.jsonl`.

## Verification results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| MEMORY/USER blocks appear once | 86% (1,892/2,200) and 94% (1,287/1,375) |
| `oum_session_search` | returned historical sessions for "PigeonHater calibration margin histogram" |
| `oum_memory` add/replace/remove | add applied, remove applied, usage returned to baseline |

## Remaining step

The running service caches the plugin set, so the TUI keeps the old set until:

```sh
opencode service restart
```

New locations already load OUM (verified with a private server), so the restart
only refreshes sessions that were open during the switch.

## Preconditions (historical)

1. Update OpenCode to the target V2 release.
2. Verify the four unknowns from the design.
3. Back up:
   - `~/.config/opencode/memories/`
   - `~/.agents/skills/`
   - `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`

## Import canonical memory

`bun run scripts/migrate.ts` (dry run) and `--apply` (copy). Additive: it refuses
a non-empty target unless `--force`, backs up first, and verifies entries.

## Skills

No move. Both plugins use `~/.agents/skills`. OUM reads the existing library and
indexes it for dedupe; it does not rewrite user-authored skills.

## Coexistence

Do not run both memory plugins at once. Two plugins would inject two memory
blocks and write to the same files.

- Disable `opencode-hermes` in `opencode.jsonc`.
- Enable `openultramem`.
- Restart the background service (`opencode service restart`).
- OUM refuses to inject if it detects `opencode-hermes` in the active plugin
  list, unless `coexistence: true`.

## State

OUM indexes V2 sessions only. There is no V1 backfill. Old V1 history remains in
the host database but is not searchable through OUM.

## Rollback

- Disable `openultramem`.
- Re-enable `opencode-hermes`.
- Restart the service.
- The old files are untouched; only OUM's new data root needs removal for a clean
  rollback. The backup directory holds the pre-migration state.

## Non-goals

- Importing the old embeddings store.
- Rewriting existing skills.
- Migrating V1 session history.

# Releasing

Semantic versioning, annotated tags, one tag per shipped state. The tag, the
`package.json` version, and `src/version.ts` must always agree —
`test/version.test.ts` fails the suite if they drift.

## Checklist

1. `bun test` and `bunx tsc --noEmit` are green.
2. `bun run scripts/bench.ts` still passes the retrieval budget.
3. Bump the version in three places: `package.json`, `src/version.ts`, and a new
   `CHANGELOG.md` section.
4. Commit: `chore(release): vX.Y.Z`.
5. Annotated tag with the short feature list as the message:
   `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "vX.Y.Z"` then `git push origin main --follow-tags`.
6. Create the GitHub release from the tag; the body is the changelog section.

## Version rules

- `0.x`: the plugin surface may change; `x` increments for breaking changes to
  tools, config, or on-disk layout.
- Patch releases fix behaviour without changing the tool surface.
- No pre-1.0 `1.0.0` claims: 1.0 waits for the learn module and skill authoring
  to be live, not merely designed.

# `state.db` schema and retrieval

Status: design. Not implemented.

`state.db` is a **derived index** over OpenCode's own session database. It is
disposable: deleting it loses no history. The host database is opened read-only
and never written.

Path: `<dataRoot>/state.db`, with `<dataRoot>` defaulting to
`~/.local/share/opencode/oum`. WAL, `synchronous=NORMAL`, `busy_timeout=5000`.

## DDL

```sql
CREATE TABLE meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);

CREATE TABLE sessions(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  project_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  directory TEXT NOT NULL,
  title TEXT,
  parent_id TEXT,
  model TEXT,
  created INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated INTEGER NOT NULL,
  hidden INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  indexed_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE messages(
  rid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
  role TEXT NOT NULL,          -- user | assistant | tool | synthetic
  created INTEGER NOT NULL,
  tool_name TEXT,
  chars INTEGER NOT NULL,
  indexed_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- Word index: BM25 and phrase precision. Contentless: tokens only.
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE messages_fts USING fts5(
  text,
  content='', contentless_delete=1,
  tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'
);

-- Substring index: literal matching and high recall. Contentless: tokens only.
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE messages_fts_tri USING fts5(
  text,
  content='', contentless_delete=1,
  tokenize='trigram'
);

CREATE INDEX messages_session_seq ON messages(session_id, seq);
CREATE INDEX messages_created ON messages(created);
```

Full text is hydrated from `opencode.db` by message ID. The indexes store tokens,
not message bodies.

## Ingest mapping (V2 only)

Source: `session_v2` + `session_message`.

| `session_message.type` | Stored as | Text |
|---|---|---|
| `user` | `user` | `data.text` |
| `assistant` | `assistant` | text blocks |
| assistant tool block | `tool` | tool name + bounded input/output |
| `synthetic` | `synthetic` | `data.text` unless it is an OUM/provider recall note |
| `system`, `idle`, `location-switched` | skipped | — |

- Reasoning blocks are skipped.
- `session_v2.parent_id` children get `hidden = 1`; searchable only with
  `include_children: true`.
- Every message upsert deletes and reinserts its FTS rows by `rid` in the same
  transaction.

Watermark: `(time_created, id)` in `meta`. Each sync re-scans a 60-second
overlap window. Upserts are idempotent by message ID.

Deletions: purge on `session.deleted` and on a full reconcile pass.

## Search

1. Sync (bounded, default 250 ms).
2. Word FTS and trigram FTS in parallel, top 50 each.
3. Reciprocal rank fusion (`k = 60`), dedupe by message ID, recency tiebreak.
4. Hydrate top hits; build snippets.
5. If sync fails or the index is empty, fall back to a bounded `LIKE` query over
   extracted host text.

Modes: `broad` (OR terms, default) and `exact` (phrase / substring).

## Invariants

- `opencode.db` is attached read-only (`mode=ro`).
- FTS tables are contentless; no duplicated message bodies.
- A vector/embedding index, if added later, records `model_id` and `dims`; a
  model change triggers a rebuild, not a silent mismatch.
- `state.db` corruption is recoverable by deletion and rebuild.

## Rebuild

```text
1. Stop the plugin.
2. Move state.db aside.
3. Start OUM; the first sync backfills V2 sessions.
```

No V1 session backfill is planned. Old V1 history stays in the host database but
is not indexed.

# Pre-build verification — 2026-10-27

Answers to the four unknowns in [BUILD.md](BUILD.md), measured on **OpenCode
2.2.0** (Bun-shipped binary) with `@opencode/plugin` **2.2.0**. Probe: a throwaway
Promise plugin registered a namespaced Code Mode tool, subscribed to the event
stream, and called `ctx.experimental.generate.text`; a `opencode run` session then
invoked the tool. Probe removed after the run.

## 1. `session.execution.*` delivery

Exist and are delivered live:

```
session.execution.started    {"sessionID":"ses_e810..."}
session.execution.succeeded  {"sessionID":"ses_e810..."}
```

- The event catalog also carries `session.compaction.started|delta|ended|failed`,
  `session.tool.called|success|failed`, `session.step.*`, `session.idle`.
- Envelope is `durability: "durable"` with `aggregateID` and `seq`.
- **But there is no replay.** `event_sequence` tracks per-session sequence numbers
  (up to 706), while the `event` table holds only five legacy rows and zero
  execution events. Durable events are not retained host-side, so a missed event
  cannot be recovered by seq.
- Consequence: the **next-prompt fallback is mandatory**, exactly as designed.
  Do not build a replay reader; there is nothing to replay.

## 2. `ctx.tool.transform` + namespace + `codemode: true`

Works as designed.

```
tool.list: 25 tools, ours = [{"id":"oumprobe_echo","options":{"namespace":"oumprobe","codemode":true}}]
```

The model was given `tools.oumprobe.echo({ text: "hello" })` and called it through
Code Mode (`session.tool.called` shows the JS source, `executed: false`). Effective
ID is `namespace_name`; the namespace description and per-tool `options` survive.

## 3. `generate.text` with a pinned model

Works, and fails visibly.

```
generate.ok       {"ms":1250,"text":"PROBE-OK"}          # opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash
generate.badmodel {"message":"Model not found: opencode-go/does-not-exist-probe"}
```

`ctx.generate.text` still exists but is deprecated in favour of
`ctx.experimental.generate.text({ model: { providerID, id }, prompt })`.

## 4. Read-only attach of the live WAL `opencode.db`

Works. `sqlite3 "file:...opencode.db?mode=ro"` read schema and rows while the
service was writing, and `bun:sqlite` `new Database(path, { readonly: true })` is
already used in production by `opencode-hermes` against the same file.

Host schema matches the design:

```
session_v2(id, project_id, parent_id, directory, title, model, time_created, time_updated, ...)
session_message(id, session_id, type, seq, time_created, data)   -- 7,051 rows
types: assistant 5472, user 767, synthetic 409, idle 265, location-switched 74, system 64
```

## Runtime facts

- Plugins execute inside the Bun binary, so `bun:sqlite` is available to the plugin
  itself. Local `bun` 1.4.2 is installed for tests.
- `ctx.options`, `ctx.location.{directory,project.id}` are available in `setup`.
- `session.hook("context", event)` gives `sessionID`, `agent`, `model`, mutable
  `system[]`, `tools`, `messages`, and `options` on every model call. This is the
  injection point for the frozen memory snapshot.
- V2 event names use dots; subscribe with `{ types: [...] }`.

## Still unmeasured

- Event **miss rate** in ordinary use (needs a live correlation over days, not a
  single probe). The fallback covers it; the event log makes the rate measurable.
